title: AI Explorers
short_description: Meet AI, spot patterns, and dream up your own helpful invention.
description: Meet AI, spot patterns, and dream up your own helpful invention.

blocks.text: AI is software that learns patterns from examples. It can suggest a song or help recognise a picture. It does not think or feel like you do.
Look around with a grown-up. Find one thing that might use AI. Explain what examples it could learn from.
A pattern is something that repeats. AI uses patterns in its training examples to make a prediction. A prediction can be wrong.
Draw a circle, square, circle, square. What comes next? Make a second pattern and ask someone to predict it.
Good inventions start with a problem. AI should help people, and a person should check important answers. Never share private information with a chatbot.
On paper, design a robot that helps with one small chore. Label its input, what it does, and how a grown-up checks it.

title: Your First Coding Adventure
short_description: Turn simple instructions into something wonderfully your own.
description: Turn simple instructions into something wonderfully your own.

blocks.text: A program is a list of instructions. Order matters: put your socks on before your shoes. A computer needs clear steps.
Write four instructions to draw a house. Ask a grown-up to follow them exactly. Improve any unclear step.
A loop repeats an instruction. Instead of writing clap five times, you can say repeat clap five times.
Create a dance with three moves. Repeat the dance twice. How many moves did you perform altogether?
A bug is a mistake in instructions. Debugging means finding it and trying a fix. All programmers debug.
Write instructions to move across a paper grid. Try them with a coin. Find and fix one step that goes wrong.

title: Make Your Imagination Pop
short_description: Play with colours, shapes, and stories. Create a character that is all you.
description: Play with colours, shapes, and stories. Create a character that is all you.

blocks.text: Artists combine simple shapes to build pictures. A circle and two triangles can become a friendly cat.
Draw a character using three kinds of shapes. Give it a name.
Colours can make a picture feel bright, calm, or exciting. Different people can feel differently about the same colour.
Choose three colours for your character. Explain why you chose each one.
A story has a beginning, something that happens, and an ending. Pictures can tell a story too.
Draw three pictures showing your character helping a friend. Share the story with your grown-up.

title: Internet Superpowers
short_description: Learn to explore, pause, and make kinder choices online.
description: Learn to explore, pause, and make kinder choices online.

blocks.text: Your address, passwords, school details, and private pictures should not be shared online. Ask a trusted grown-up when you are unsure.
Make a pretend profile for an imaginary superhero. Include a nickname, favourite colour, and hobby. Leave out private details.
Messages and websites are not always what they seem. Surprising prizes and urgent demands are a reason to pause.
With a grown-up, invent a suspicious prize message. Name two clues that mean you should ask for help.
There is a real person behind a screen. If something makes you uncomfortable, stop and speak to a trusted adult.
Write a kind response to an imaginary friend whose drawing did not turn out as planned.

title: Big Ideas, Little Apps
short_description: Plan an app, write clear prompts, and learn to check what AI creates.
description: Plan an app, write clear prompts, and learn to check what AI creates.

blocks.text: Before you ask AI to write code, describe who your app helps and what one task it should do.
Sketch a homework checklist on paper with a title, input, and list. Explain how someone would use it.
A clear prompt describes the goal, constraints, and expected result. AI-generated code may contain mistakes. A grown-up should help choose a suitable tool.
Write a prompt for your checklist: what should happen when someone adds a task? What should happen if it is empty?
Testing means trying expected and unexpected actions. Never put private information or passwords into a coding prompt.
Try your paper app with a friend. Ask them to add an empty task and a very long task. Write down two improvements.

title: Your Digital Story Studio
short_description: From a tiny idea to a story worth sharing with your family.
description: From a tiny idea to a story worth sharing with your family.

blocks.text: A memorable story gives its character something to want and a problem to solve.
Invent a character, one goal, and one problem. Write a sentence for each.
A storyboard plans a story in pictures. Each frame shows an important moment.
Divide a page into four frames. Sketch your beginning, problem, attempt, and ending.
Creators respect other people’s work. Use your own drawings or material you have permission to use.
Make a title and final frame for your story. Add your creator nickname and credits for any borrowed work.
